title: How do animals regrow their limbs? And why can't humans do it? - Jessica Whited
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】動物如何重新長出四肢？而人類為什麼做不到呢？ - 傑西卡懷特（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: For some animals, losing a limb is a decidedly permanent affair.
cues.en: For some animals, losing a limb is a decidedly permanent affair.
cues.zh: 對於某些動物來說，斷肢 是永久且無法改變的事。

cues.text: But for salamanders, particularly axolotls, amputation is just a temporary affliction.
cues.en: But for salamanders, particularly axolotls, amputation is just a temporary affliction.
cues.zh: 但對於蠑螈而言， 特別是墨西哥鈍口螈， 斷肢只是種暫時性的麻煩。

cues.text: Not only can they grow back entire limbs in as little as six weeks,
cues.en: Not only can they grow back entire limbs in as little as six weeks,
cues.zh: 牠們不僅可以在短短六週內 就把斷掉的部分完全長回來，

cues.text: they can also regenerate heart and even brain tissue.
cues.en: they can also regenerate heart and even brain tissue.
cues.zh: 牠們不僅可以在短短六週內 就把斷掉的部分完全長回來， 連心臟，甚至大腦組織都可以再生。

cues.text: So how does this astonishing adaptation work?
cues.en: So how does this astonishing adaptation work?
cues.zh: 這種驚人的適應機制是如何運作的？

cues.text: Regardless of regeneration, every limbed creature had to grow their arms and legs at some point.
cues.en: Regardless of regeneration, every limbed creature had to grow their arms and legs at some point.
cues.zh: 先不談再生， 每一種有四肢的生物 都會在某個時點長出手腳來。

cues.text: And whether that process starts in the womb or the world, it almost always begins with little bumps called limb buds.
cues.en: And whether that process starts in the womb or the world, it almost always begins with little bumps called limb buds.
cues.zh: 無論這個過程是從子宮裡 就開始還是出世後才開始， 幾乎都始於一種小突起，叫做肢芽。

cues.text: These buds are full of progenitor cells— a cornucopia of cell types that can differentiate into various tissues,
cues.en: These buds are full of progenitor cells— a cornucopia of cell types that can differentiate into various tissues,
cues.zh: 肢芽裡面滿是先驅細胞， 也就是可以分化成各種組織的 多種型別的細胞，

cues.text: including muscles, cartilage, ligaments, and tendons.
cues.en: including muscles, cartilage, ligaments, and tendons.
cues.zh: 包括肌肉、軟骨、韌帶，和肌腱。

cues.text: Some of these progenitors are stem cells, capable of developing into a range of specialized cells and tissues,
cues.en: Some of these progenitors are stem cells, capable of developing into a range of specialized cells and tissues,
cues.zh: 有一些先驅細胞是幹細胞， 能夠發展成多種 專門化的細胞和組織，

cues.text: while others are merely derived from stem cells.
cues.en: while others are merely derived from stem cells.
cues.zh: 其他的則只是由幹細胞衍生出來的。

cues.text: But in either case, the progenitors differentiate and multiply rapidly
cues.en: But in either case, the progenitors differentiate and multiply rapidly
cues.zh: 但不論是哪一種先驅細胞， 都會隨著肢芽的發展 而快速分化和增殖。

cues.text: as the limb bud develops.
cues.en: as the limb bud develops.
cues.zh: 而快速分化和增殖。

cues.text: Nerves grow into the limb from nearby cell bodies and a network of blood vessels form which fuel the process with oxygen.
cues.en: Nerves grow into the limb from nearby cell bodies and a network of blood vessels form which fuel the process with oxygen.
cues.zh: 神經會從附近的細胞體 生長到四肢裡面， 還會形成血管網路， 為這個過程提供氧氣。

cues.text: Eventually, that tiny bud grows into a full infant limb.
cues.en: Eventually, that tiny bud grows into a full infant limb.
cues.zh: 最終，小芽長大成為 完整的新生四肢。

cues.text: Most salamanders, including axolotls, develop their limbs in the same way.
cues.en: Most salamanders, including axolotls, develop their limbs in the same way.
cues.zh: 大部分的蠑螈，包括墨西哥鈍口螈， 用同樣的方式長出牠們的肢體。

cues.text: But unlike other animals, they can also start this process all over again
cues.en: But unlike other animals, they can also start this process all over again
cues.zh: 但和其他動物不同的是， 如果有需要，牠們可以 一而再再而三啟動這個過程。

cues.text: if they need to.
cues.en: if they need to.
cues.zh: 如果有需要，牠們可以 一而再再而三啟動這個過程。

cues.text: When salamanders lose a limb, surrounding skin cells quickly surge across the wound’s surface.
cues.en: When salamanders lose a limb, surrounding skin cells quickly surge across the wound’s surface.
cues.zh: 蠑螈失去一肢時， 周圍的皮膚細胞 會迅速覆蓋傷口表面。

cues.text: This new layer of skin is called the wound epidermis,
cues.en: This new layer of skin is called the wound epidermis,
cues.zh: 這層新的皮膚稱為傷口表皮，

cues.text: and once established, it signals cells in the underlying limb stump
cues.en: and once established, it signals cells in the underlying limb stump
cues.zh: 形成之後，它會傳送訊號 給皮膚下殘肢中的細胞，

cues.text: to undergo something called dedifferentiation.
cues.en: to undergo something called dedifferentiation.
cues.zh: 進行一個叫做「去分化」的過程。

cues.text: This process reverts nearby cells from fully developed limb tissues
cues.en: This process reverts nearby cells from fully developed limb tissues
cues.zh: 這個過程會將附近的細胞還原， 從發展完成的肢體組織 回復到較早期、尚未分化成 有專門功能的先驅細胞。

cues.text: back into earlier, less specialized progenitor cells.
cues.en: back into earlier, less specialized progenitor cells.
cues.zh: 這個過程會將附近的細胞還原， 從發展完成的肢體組織 回復到較早期、尚未分化成 有專門功能的先驅細胞。

cues.text: At the same time, the peripheral nervous system fires up stem cells
cues.en: At the same time, the peripheral nervous system fires up stem cells
cues.zh: 同時， 周邊神經系統會啟動 蠑螈全身的幹細胞。

cues.text: throughout the salamander’s body.
cues.en: throughout the salamander’s body.
cues.zh: 周邊神經系統會啟動 蠑螈全身的幹細胞。

cues.text: This would be impossible for most multicellular organisms, whose stem cells typically lose their regenerative capacity with age.
cues.en: This would be impossible for most multicellular organisms, whose stem cells typically lose their regenerative capacity with age.
cues.zh: 大部分的多細胞生物 都做不到這一點， 牠們的幹細胞通常會 隨著年齡失去再生能力。

cues.text: But when salamander stem cells near the injury get the right signal,
cues.en: But when salamander stem cells near the injury get the right signal,
cues.zh: 但當蠑螈傷口附近的幹細胞 接收到對的訊號時，

cues.text: they reactivate and start multiplying.
cues.en: they reactivate and start multiplying.
cues.zh: 它們會重新啟動並開始增殖。

cues.text: Researchers don’t know what ratio of stem cells and dedifferentiated progenitor cells regeneration requires.
cues.en: Researchers don’t know what ratio of stem cells and dedifferentiated progenitor cells regeneration requires.
cues.zh: 研究人員還不知道再生需要 多少比例的幹細胞 和去分化先驅細胞。

cues.text: But we do know these cells come together to form the most important part of the process: the blastema.
cues.en: But we do know these cells come together to form the most important part of the process: the blastema.
cues.zh: 但我們確實知道 這些細胞結合起來形成 這個過程中最重要的部分： 胚基。

cues.text: This structure is almost identical to a limb bud— the primary difference is that it’s made of recycled, repurposed cells,
cues.en: This structure is almost identical to a limb bud— the primary difference is that it’s made of recycled, repurposed cells,
cues.zh: 它的結構和肢芽幾乎一模一樣—— 主要的差別在於胚基 是回收後再利用的細胞所構成，

cues.text: and potentially reserved cells, rather than completely new ones.
cues.en: and potentially reserved cells, rather than completely new ones.
cues.zh: 以及可能被儲備下來的細胞， 而不是全新的細胞。

cues.text: Beyond that, blastemas and limb buds have the same mission:
cues.en: Beyond that, blastemas and limb buds have the same mission:
cues.zh: 除了這個差異，胚基 和肢芽都具有相同的任務：

cues.text: to make thousands of new cells and organize them into the muscle, bone, skin, and nerve tissue
cues.en: to make thousands of new cells and organize them into the muscle, bone, skin, and nerve tissue
cues.zh: 製造數千個新細胞，並將它們組織 成為有功能的四肢需要的肌肉、 骨頭、皮膚，及神經組織。

cues.text: required for a functional limb.
cues.en: required for a functional limb.
cues.zh: 成為有功能的四肢需要的肌肉、 骨頭、皮膚，及神經組織。

cues.text: As this process unfolds, nerves and blood vessels spanning the injury site
cues.en: As this process unfolds, nerves and blood vessels spanning the injury site
cues.zh: 隨著這個過程發展， 分佈在受傷部位的神經和血管

cues.text: transmit nutrition and oxygen.
cues.en: transmit nutrition and oxygen.
cues.zh: 會遞送營養和氧氣。

cues.text: Over several weeks, the stump will steadily grow a miniature limb with translucent skin.
cues.en: Over several weeks, the stump will steadily grow a miniature limb with translucent skin.
cues.zh: 在幾週內，殘肢會穩定地 長出小型肢體， 帶有透明的皮膚。

cues.text: And when the process is complete, not only will the limb match the rest of the salamander,
cues.en: And when the process is complete, not only will the limb match the rest of the salamander,
cues.zh: 此過程完成後， 重新長出來的腳 不僅能匹配蠑螈的其他部位，

cues.text: there won't even be a scar.
cues.en: there won't even be a scar.
cues.zh: 還不會留下疤痕。

cues.text: The relationship between scarring and regeneration is just one of this processes’ many mysteries.
cues.en: The relationship between scarring and regeneration is just one of this processes’ many mysteries.
cues.zh: 形成疤痕和再生之間的關係 只是這個過程的許多奧秘之一。

cues.text: Scientists are still tracking salamander cells on the molecular level
cues.en: Scientists are still tracking salamander cells on the molecular level
cues.zh: 科學家仍在從分子層面 追蹤蠑螈的細胞，

cues.text: to determine how they revert from a mature stage into a regenerative one.
cues.en: to determine how they revert from a mature stage into a regenerative one.
cues.zh: 以確定這些細胞如何 從成熟階段回復到再生階段。

cues.text: And research into transplanting blastema cells investigates how other animals might replicate this reconstructive wizardry.
cues.en: And research into transplanting blastema cells investigates how other animals might replicate this reconstructive wizardry.
cues.zh: 移植胚基細胞的研究所探究的是 其他動物要如何複製這種重建奇蹟。

cues.text: We also don’t understand how salamanders’ bodies know what part of the limb has been lost or how much needs to be regrown.
cues.en: We also don’t understand how salamanders’ bodies know what part of the limb has been lost or how much needs to be regrown.
cues.zh: 我們也不明白蠑螈的身體怎麼會知道 斷掉的是腳的哪個部分 或者需要重新生長多少。 ［左臂：施工中］

cues.text: One theory is that blastema cells have a form of positional memory,
cues.en: One theory is that blastema cells have a form of positional memory,
cues.zh: ［左臂：施工中］ 有種理論認為胚基細胞 具有某種形式的位置記憶，

cues.text: allowing them to determine how much to grow in relation to one another.
cues.en: allowing them to determine how much to grow in relation to one another.
cues.zh: 讓它們能夠根據彼此的比例， 確定該生長多少。

cues.text: And it’s equally important to understand how these limbs know when to stop growing
cues.en: And it’s equally important to understand how these limbs know when to stop growing
cues.zh: 同等重要的是：要了解 這些肢體怎麼知道何時該停止生長，

cues.text: to prevent overdevelopment, like in cancerous tumors.
cues.en: to prevent overdevelopment, like in cancerous tumors.
cues.zh: 以預防過度生長， 如癌症的腫瘤細胞那樣。

cues.text: But one of regenerations essential ingredients doesn’t belong solely
cues.en: But one of regenerations essential ingredients doesn’t belong solely
cues.zh: 但再生的要件—— 胚基——並非蠑螈獨有。

cues.text: to salamanders: the blastema.
cues.en: to salamanders: the blastema.
cues.zh: 胚基——並非蠑螈獨有。

cues.text: Deer antlers use a similar healing tissue to regenerate each year,
cues.en: Deer antlers use a similar healing tissue to regenerate each year,
cues.zh: 鹿角就會使用類似的 癒合組織每年再生，

cues.text: even though their skin scars like ours.
cues.en: even though their skin scars like ours.
cues.zh: 不過鹿的皮膚和我們的 一樣會留下疤痕。

cues.text: Spiny mice can also restore skin, hair, and some other appendages scar-free.
cues.en: Spiny mice can also restore skin, hair, and some other appendages scar-free.
cues.zh: 棘鼠也可以讓皮膚、毛髮，及其他 一些凸出於軀幹外的部位復元， 且不留下疤痕。

cues.text: And even humans can regenerate the tips of our fingers and toes
cues.en: And even humans can regenerate the tips of our fingers and toes
cues.zh: 就連人類的 指尖和趾尖也可以 用非常類似的方式再生，

cues.text: in a surprisingly similar manner.
cues.en: in a surprisingly similar manner.
cues.zh: 指尖和趾尖也可以 用非常類似的方式再生，

cues.text: We still don’t know whether this ability is tied to our shared ancestry with salamanders
cues.en: We still don’t know whether this ability is tied to our shared ancestry with salamanders
cues.zh: 我們還不知道這種能力是來自於 我們和蠑螈的共同祖先，

cues.text: or fueled by distinct biological mechanisms.
cues.en: or fueled by distinct biological mechanisms.
cues.zh: 或者是由不同的生物機制所驅動。

cues.text: But with time and research, who knows what evolutionary knowledge we might grow back.
cues.en: But with time and research, who knows what evolutionary knowledge we might grow back.
cues.zh: 但隨時間和研究， 誰又知道我們可能會 長回哪些進化知識。
